chapter: The union and the 1920s-30s band scene
title: Princess Belle, the solo pianist at the Apex
summary: Howard remembers Princess Belle, an older woman pianist who played alone at the Apex and taught him a lot when he played with her.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What was Los Angeles like when you first got here?

When I first got here? Oh, all I know was, they had somebody to be a -- something like a -- it was nothing, just like nothing. They had an entertainer, something. Now, that's Princess Belle. We forgot all about her.
Who was Princess Belle?
She belonged to the union. And she played a piano that you never heard in your life. Beautiful. You know her.
I just heard the name. I don't think I ever heard her play.
Well, oh, boy, she could play. Right now, you don't hear nothing of her. I wish you could get some of her renditions of different things.
Did she make records?
Pardon?
Did she make records?
No.
Where did she work here in Los Angeles?
Down at the Apex.
Oh.
Down there.
Did she work alone or did she have a rhythm section with her?

Worked alone. Well, she worked with me for awhile. I got a chance to play with her nights. And I was glad to play with her because she was teaching me a lot of things. Sure, I got a chance to learn a lot.
Was she older than you?
Oh, yes, a little older. When she passed away, I think I --no, I won't say that because I don't know how old I was. But I know she was older than me.
Wasn't that a little unusual, for there to be a woman solo musician appearing at a club?
Uh-huh.
There weren't others, or very many others. Can you remember any others in Los Angeles?
No, not too many. I might think of some others, if you shut the machine off and give me a chance to think some, and I can think of something else that would be more --
(Recording interrupted.)
